posts.hook: Most of a paver patio is under the pavers.
body: From the top down: pavers with sand swept into the joints, a thin layer of bedding sand, at least 4 inches of compacted stone base, then firm, compacted soil, with fabric between the base and the soil where the ground stays wet. An edge restraint keeps the pavers from creeping, and the surface falls away from the house so water runs off.
When pavers sink or shift, look at the base first. The 4-inch figure is the Concrete Masonry and Hardscapes Association's minimum for patios on well-drained soil.
posts.cta: Thinking about a patio this winter? Text (843) 998-5593.

slides.title: What's under a paver patio
slides.source: Base depth: CMHA Tech Note PAV-TEC-002
slides.alt: Section drawing: pavers, sand, a 4-inch compacted base and soil, sloping away from a house.

slides.title: Four things that keep a patio flat
items: A compacted stone base, at least 4 inches deep
Fabric under the base where the ground stays wet
An edge restraint at every open side
A slope away from the house, so water runs off

posts.hook: Before you cut down a tree in Mount Pleasant, measure it.
body: On a residential lot the Town protects trees 16 inches or more across, measured 4 1/2 feet off the ground, and pines from 24 inches. A short list of species, sweet gum among them, never needs a permit.

The request goes through the Town's online permit system and costs $50. Take a protected tree down without one and the Town fines both the homeowner and whoever cut it. That's why we ask about the permit before we schedule any tree work.
posts.cta: The full answer, with the Town's own rules, is on our website under Guides.

slides.sub: Usually, yes. Here's how to tell.

posts.hook: If water sits against your house after it rains, check which way the ground slopes.
body: Building code asks for the ground to fall at least 6 inches in the first 10 feet away from a house (International Residential Code R401.3). When it slopes toward the house instead, rainwater runs back to the foundation.
Regrading moves soil from the high side to the low side and packs it, so the finished ground falls away from the house.
posts.cta: Not sure which way yours runs? Text us a photo after the next rain: (843) 998-5593.

slides.alt: Video: a drawing of ground regraded to fall away from a house.

posts.hook: Does your yard hold water for days after a storm?
body: Usually it's the grade. The ground holds water in a low spot or sends it toward the house, and the Lowcountry's high water table leaves it nowhere to soak in.
Where there's enough fall, we regrade. Where there isn't, a swale or a French drain carries the water to somewhere it's allowed to go.
posts.cta: Send us a photo of the standing water: (843) 998-5593.

posts.hook: Fall is the best season to plant shrubs here. Here's how deep they should go.
body: Clemson Extension's advice: dig the hole two to five times wider than the root ball but no deeper, set the top roots level with the ground or slightly above it, backfill with the soil that came out, and finish with 2 to 3 inches of mulch kept off the stems.

posts.hook: Thinking about new sod? In Charleston, plan it for spring.
body: Clemson Extension says sod is best laid in mid to late spring or in the fall, early enough to root before cold weather. With cold weather coming, spring is the next good window.

Which grass comes down to sun. St. Augustine takes the most shade but still needs 4 to 6 hours of direct sun, zoysia does well in sun or part shade, centipede is the low-upkeep choice for open sun away from salt, and Bermuda needs full sun.

slides.title: When should sod go down in Charleston?
slides.sub: Mid to late spring, or early fall.
slides.alt: When should sod go down in Charleston? Mid to late spring, or early fall.

slides.title: Which grass, by how much sun
items: St. Augustine: most shade, still needs 4 to 6 hours of sun
Zoysia: sun or part shade
Centipede: low upkeep, open sun, away from salt
Bermuda: full sun only
slides.alt: St. Augustine for shade, zoysia sun or part shade, centipede open sun, Bermuda full sun.

alternates.hook: Grind the stump or pull it out? It depends on what goes there next.
body: Grind it if the spot will be lawn or a bed. Grinding takes the stump below the surface and leaves the roots to rot.
Pull it if anything will be built or dug there. The excavator lifts the stump and root ball out whole, and the hole is backfilled and packed.
alternates.cta: Have a stump in the way? Text a photo to (843) 998-5593.

slides.title: Grind the stump, or pull it out?
slides.sub: It depends on what goes there next.
slides.alt: Grind the stump, or pull it out? It depends on what goes there next.

slides.title: The short version
items: A lawn or a bed going there: grind it
A patio, a pad or digging going there: pull it
Grinding leaves the roots to rot in place
Pulling takes the root ball out; the hole is backfilled and packed
slides.alt: Lawn or bed: grind it. Patio or digging: pull it, then backfill and pack.

alternates.hook: Swale or French drain? It depends how much fall the yard has.
body: A swale is a shallow, grassy dip that carries water across the surface. A French drain is a trench lined with fabric and filled with stone around a perforated pipe, for where the ground is too flat to move water on top. Either one has to run to somewhere the water is allowed to go.
